text:
maria: Hey @people-ops — need help adding a dependent who's a full-time student studying abroad (UK). She turned 23 this month. Can I add her as a dependent under student status while she's overseas? Also asking about retroactive coverage for a clinic visit last month that I paid for out of pocket. What docs do you need?

sam: Hi Maria — short answer: usually possible if they meet plan's dependent rules (full-time student). We'll need proof of enrollment + relationship + ID. For retro coverage we need the enrollment form + clinic invoice + payment receipt + a retro request explanation. DM me basic details and we'll start a case.

maria: Thanks. Any ETA? the clinic charged £180 (~$240) on 2026-02-10 and I have the receipt. Hoping to avoid eating that cost.

jamal (Benefits Team): Hey Maria — here's what carriers typically require for student dependents abroad: 1) Completed Dependent Enrollment Form (PDF) — attach to email; 2) Official university enrollment letter on school letterhead showing full-time status and dates; 3) Copy of passport + visa page; 4) Proof of relationship (birth certificate for sibling); 5) Proof of overseas residence (utility, lease, or bank statement) OR a notarized residency affidavit; 6) Itemized clinic invoice + proof of payment; 7) Retro enrollment explanation letter requesting effective date, signed by employee. Please send all docs to benefits@redwood.com with subject line: "Retro Enroll Request - Maria [last name]".

benefits-bot: Automated: Dependent Enrollment Form v2 -> https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/dependent-enroll. Carrier processing for retro adds: typically 4–8 weeks. For medical emergencies/appeals you can request expedited review — include "URGENT: Retro Enroll" in subject.

lila: Also confirm whether the clinic is in-network for that country. International clinics are often out-of-network which affects reimbursement. Use carrier provider search: https://www.carrier-example.com/provider-search (set location = United Kingdom). If you paid, keep itemized charges with any CPT/diagnosis codes — that helps claims.

maria: The receipt is in Portuguese (clinic handles tourists). Is a translation required?

jamal (Benefits Team): We accept certified translations. A notarized translation or certified translator statement is fine. If you want faster handling, upload original + translation together.

sam: Once we get the docs, we file the retro enrollment with the carrier and request claims reprocessing. Carriers can consider dates up to 12 months back depending on terms, but reimbursement isn't guaranteed. Expect initial confirmation from us within 2–3 business days that we submitted to the carrier; carrier adjudication is the 4–8 week window.

maria: Do I get a digital ID card immediately after you submit? I need something for future appointments.

benefits-bot: Digital ID cards are issued by the carrier after enrollment confirmation. For retro requests, cards will reflect the approved effective date. Temporary proof: benefits@redwood.com can issue an internal confirmation letter (turnaround 1–2 business days) you can show to providers in the meantime.

lila: If the clinic might require pre-authorization for follow-ups, we can share an emergent pre-auth template and call script for the carrier's international line. Ping me after you send docs and I'll DM the template.

maria: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll compile the passport scans, uni letter, clinic invoice and translation and email benefits tonight.

sam: Appreciate it — we'll pick this up as soon as the email hits the queue. :thumbsup:

jamal (Benefits Team): FYI, include currency conversion (official bank exchange screenshot or a note) for the paid amount to speed claims.

maria: Will do.
